items.grid: E237's 30 states in E237's World (through E242's): the 15 '<state>_scaled' (E147's saved update times E237's c per task, experiments/key_grid/results/stage0.json) and their 15 'random_<state>' (E237's Gaussian direction at the state's per-matrix norms, times the same c), each on its state's own D at the last position. readings.E_b_K: commute.stand_in.explained_share(num, den, dd, K and changed), K by commute.needed.needed_set with E268's settings at the last read position; 1 when K has no changed member (flagged empty_K)
readings.E_b_Kstar: the same over the item's saved K* (commute.kstar_vpd.saved_k_star), where one exists
readings.too_small: |K| < too_small: the item reads 'too small to read'

rules.R0a: Stage 0 stops the job on any argmax change under the identity interchange (x' = x) on the control's D (first 64 windows, three subcomponents and the remainder of every matrix, last position). Its largest logit deviation is the floor, recorded, not barred (E268 R0a)
rules.R0b: Stage 0 stops the job unless the do-nothing (F = M) has no changed variable, every dd exactly 0.0 and E_b over K exactly 1.0 (E268 R0b; any K, as K and changed is empty)
rules.R0c: Every random item stops the job unless its featurization has E237's saved n_vars and n_changed and its c is E237's (experiments/key_grid/results/vpd/random_<state>.json): a guard on the construction (wrong seed index, wrong c, wrong state), not a noise floor

expected.stage0: identity: 0 argmax changes, largest logit deviation about 5e-5 or below (E268 measured 5.1e-5); do-nothing: 0 changed, dd max 0.0, E_b over K 1.0; time per item about 500 s on an H100 (38,938 variables x 256 pairs at about 20k cases/s, E268)
expected.e62: descriptive: rival A reads E_b over K of copy minus lookup (mean over seeds 0-2) at least rival_gap; rival B under it
expected.grid: descriptive: rival A orders the tasks as their squared-cosine R panels (copy highest, cipher lowest), each above its matched random; rival B has them within rival_gap of one another and of their randoms. Randoms expected at or under random_max
